desc:
The string num is a positive integer written with the digits 1 to 9 only. You must delete exactly one character from num, and it has to be a character equal to the digit digit. Return the largest resulting number, again as a string.

Example: num = "1231" and digit = 1 gives "231" (deleting the first 1) rather than "123".
constraints: num[i] is a digit between '1' and '9'
1 ≤ digit ≤ 9 and digit occurs at least once in num
hints: All candidates have the same length, so the largest number is also the lexicographically largest string. You could try deleting each occurrence and keep the best.

Compare the candidates from deleting two different occurrences: the strings agree up to the earlier position, so the first difference decides. What does the character right after a deleted digit do to the result?
Delete the first occurrence of digit that is followed by a larger digit, because that moves a bigger digit forward. If there is no such occurrence, delete the last occurrence.
editorial: Deleting position i makes the digit that used to be at i + 1 take its place. So compared with leaving the number alone, deleting an occurrence followed by a larger digit increases the value at that position, and the earlier such an increase happens the more it is worth. Hence the first occurrence of digit whose right neighbour is larger is the best deletion.

If no occurrence has a larger right neighbour, every deletion either lowers or keeps the digit that takes its place, and the damage is smallest when it happens as far to the right as possible, so delete the last occurrence. This is the one-digit special case of the greedy stack used for 'remove k digits'. One pass, O(n) time.
